## Controller 1.0.51 (70)
- Connect Repositories sync on their own. New commits on a linked repository's default branch reach Connect within about half a minute, and from there your GitHub mirror. Commits from your other Macs and from GitHub are fetched in the background, and a clean checkout fast-forwards. Turn it off per checkout with **Sync automatically** in Git Actions. - Encrypted repositories now open on your iPhone, Android phone and other Macs. A Mac that has a repository's key hands it over Connect's end-to-end encrypted connection when one of your devices connects to it. - **Replace History** in Git Actions deliberately rewrites a branch in Connect after an amend, rebase, squash or reset. The GitHub mirror follows with a protected force push, but only if GitHub has nothing that the replaced history didn't already have.

## Controller 1.0.51 (69)
- Connect Repositories can be end-to-end encrypted. Each repository gets its own key, wrapped separately for each of your devices; Connect stores only sealed data, a Mac without the key can be provisioned by one that has it, and removing a device rotates the key so it can't read anything new. - Pull requests flow through Connect. When a pull request is merged on GitHub, the Mac lands the merge in Connect, and open pull requests' review branches are available to every Mac through Git Actions and the review tool. - Your iPhone and Android phone can browse Connect Repositories on their own, even while every Mac is asleep: branches, files, commits and comparisons, including encrypted repositories. Find it under Settings → Connect Repos (on Android, Settings → Controller Connect → Connect Repos). - New projects created with Git get a Connect Repository by default when you're signed in, with an optional GitHub Mirror. Existing projects are unchanged. - Connect Repositories have a 5 GB storage allowance per account, and old unused data is cleaned up automatically. A full allowance shows as a clear "storage full" message.

## Controller 1.0.51 (68)
- Connect hosting is more reliable. The OpenTunnel client now follows the latest reference client: a dropped or conflicting connection, a server restart, or a temporary Cloudflare error reconnects with backoff instead of failing with "The OpenTunnel connection closed", and the Mac keeps its address instead of replacing it under connected phones. - Certificates are now renewed by OpenTunnel itself. The Mac only picks up the renewed one, so renewal no longer pauses new connections, and a failed certificate is requested again on the same address. - OpenTunnel errors now say what actually happened, for example a Cloudflare 525 during a server restart. - Connect Repositories can mirror to GitHub: the Mac mirrors a linked repository after Push to Connect and on wake, shows divergence in Git Actions, and a GitHub link can now be removed as well as changed (also through `connect_repo_github_link` with `clear: true`). - Isolated checkouts find Git LFS correctly.
